what: Several full-screen photo plates are stacked in one place with the section pinned, and with each screen of scroll the top plate is clipped away from its bottom edge upward (clip-path inset bottom 0→100%) — the clearing plate’s photo rises −15%, the plate below comes up from 15% down, the dark veil over it clears from .9→0, and the caption comes down from above (−100%). Each plate snaps over .8s. On narrow screens each plate is split into a top 60% photo and bottom 40% caption, and for plate count × screen length the pinned plate’s photo cell of the plate above is pushed up and out (the inside pushed the opposite way so it looks cut) while the caption cell drops away downward (scrub .3).

options.[data-fx-part=view]: Set of panels attached to the screen
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Stacked panels — the one behind the document sits on top and is removed first (the first panel stays)
options.[data-fx-part=media]: Photo slot inside the panel (window that gets pushed up and out on narrow screens)
options.[data-fx-part=inner]: Inside the photo frame (on narrow screens it pushes backward so the photo seems to stay in place)
options.[data-fx-part=img]: Photo moving −15% to 15% with parallax (130% height on wide screens)
options.[data-fx-part=caption]: (If present) description text — bottom left over the photo on wide screens, bottom 40% on narrow screens
options.[data-fx-part=layer]: (If present) dark layer over the lower panel — .9→0 on wide screens only
options.narrow: Width (px) at which it switches to the narrow screen, default 768
options.snap: Snap duration (s), 0 means no snap, default .8

note: The original passes ”magic” as a snap curve, but it is an unregistered name, so it runs on the GSAP default (power1.out). The plane tween likewise uses the GSAP default (power1.out · .5) with no curve or duration given, as in the original. Narrow-screen section height is --fx-count × 100svh (CSS). The wide layout in fx.css is tied to 768px, so if you change narrow, match the consuming CSS to the same width.
